biography: Xandy Negrão, a São Paulo native, discovered his passion for speed not on the karting circuits, but amidst the chaotic streets of his neighborhood. Tales abound of young Xandy, weaving his beat-up bicycle through traffic with a daring that bordered on reckless. His formal racing career began in the Copa Uno series, a far cry from the glamour of Formula 1, but a proving ground nonetheless. It was here, amidst the close-quarters racing and unpredictable handling of the humble Uno, that Negrão honed his aggressive overtaking style. A brief but promising stint with Mercedes-AMG GT3 saw flashes of brilliance, overshadowed by inconsistency and a string of costly errors. Now racing for Team Medley, Negrão is battling to stay relevant in a sport that seemingly has passed him by, a veteran clinging to the hope of rediscovering his earlier form. His family's support remains unwavering, a constant source of motivation in the face of dwindling opportunities, although whispers persist that his heart is no longer fully in the game.
drivingStyle: Negrão's driving style can be best described as 'high risk, high reward.' He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to dive down the inside of corners, often resulting in spectacular overtakes or equally spectacular crashes. Tire management is not his forte; he tends to burn through rubber early in the race, leaving him vulnerable in the closing stages. Under pressure, Negrão can either elevate his game to another level, pulling off miraculous saves and daring passes, or succumb to the pressure, making uncharacteristic mistakes that cost him dearly.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Vargas
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their Copa Uno days. Vargas, a more calculated driver, often criticized Negrão's aggressive tactics, leading to frequent on-track clashes and heated exchanges off the track.

rivalries.name: Isabela Flores
rivalries.reason: A fierce competitor in the Mercedes-AMG GT3 series. Flores, known for her clinical precision, consistently outpaced Negrão, fueling his frustration and leading to several ill-advised attempts to overtake her, often ending in collisions.

rivalries.name: Mateus Oliveira
rivalries.reason: Oliveira, a young upstart in Team Medley, has been consistently outperforming Negrão, threatening his position within the team and reigniting his competitive fire, albeit with mixed results.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Has a pre-race ritual of listening to a specific song by Sepultura at full volume to get himself 'pumped up'.
Refuses to enter the car from the left side, always insisting on entering from the right.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe. It's about pushing limits, taking chances, and sometimes, dancing on the edge of disaster."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 São Paulo Grand Prix in the Mercedes-AMG GT3 after starting from P8, a masterful drive in treacherous wet conditions showcasing his raw talent and car control.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2020 Brazilian Endurance Championship, costing Team Medley the championship title and earning him widespread criticism.
